hypothesis: Establish reference max QPS with stock config.
label: baseline

hypothesis: Socket rcvbuf overflow is the dominant loss; larger buffers absorb bursts and performance governor + no deep C-states reduces wakeup latency of named threads. Expect >10% gain if losses are burst-driven rather than pure CPU saturation.
label: rbuf16M-perfgov
host_commands: ["sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=67108864 net.core.wmem_max=67108864 net.core.rmem_default=16777216 net.core.wmem_default=16777216", "for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done", "for s in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state[2-9]/disable; do [ -e $s ] && echo 1 > $s; done; true", "systemctl restart named"]

hypothesis: With reuseport each of 32 threads gets 1/32 of traffic, so the slowest thread (sharing CPU with doubled-up NIC softirqs) overflows. A single shared socket self-balances; if contention is not dominant, max QPS rises above 700k.
label: rbuf16M-perfgov-noreuseport
host_commands: ["sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=67108864 net.core.wmem_max=67108864 net.core.rmem_default=16777216 net.core.wmem_default=16777216", "for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done", "for s in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state[2-9]/disable; do [ -e $s ] && echo 1 > $s; done; true", "systemctl restart named"]

hypothesis: irqbalance doubled queues on CPUs 4,20,24,30 and left node0's 8 physical cores carrying all softirq; named threads there fall behind and their reuseport sockets overflow. Spreading 16 queues one per physical core (CPU 0-15) evens per-core load; expect higher and less noisy max QPS than 700k.
label: rbuf16M-perfgov-irq1percore
host_commands: ["sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=67108864 net.core.wmem_max=67108864 net.core.rmem_default=16777216 net.core.wmem_default=16777216", "for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done", "for s in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state[2-9]/disable; do [ -e $s ] && echo 1 > $s; done; true", "systemctl stop irqbalance", "for q in $(seq 0 15); do irq=$(grep -E \"enp4s0f0np0-$q\\$\" /proc/interrupts | awk -F: '{print $1}' | tr -d ' '); echo $q > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; done", "systemctl restart named"]

hypothesis: Ablation: if IRQ imbalance was the real bottleneck, spreading queues alone (stock buffers, schedutil) may reach the client limit; if not, buffers/governor are needed too.
label: irq1percore-only
host_commands: ["systemctl stop irqbalance", "for q in $(seq 0 15); do irq=$(grep -E \"enp4s0f0np0-$q\\$\" /proc/interrupts | awk -F: '{print $1}' | tr -d ' '); echo $q > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; done", "systemctl restart named"]

hypothesis: Remaining losses at the client's max rate (~780k) are socket overflows from named threads short of CPU. PTI/retpoline/MDS mitigations make every syscall expensive on Ivy Bridge; mitigations=off should cut per-query CPU and push answer rate at the client limit closer to 100% (more headroom).
label: best+mitigations-off
host_commands: ["printf 'net.core.rmem_max=67108864\\nnet.core.wmem_max=67108864\\nnet.core.rmem_default=16777216\\nnet.core.wmem_default=16777216\\n' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-dnstune.conf", "printf '#!/bin/bash\\nsystemctl stop irqbalance\\nfor g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done\\nfor s in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state[2-9]/disable; do [ -e $s ] && echo 1 > $s; done\\nfor q in $(seq 0 15); do irq=$(grep -E \"enp4s0f0np0-$q\\\\$\" /proc/interrupts | awk -F: \"{print \\\\$1}\" | tr -d \" \"); [ -n \"$irq\" ] && echo $q > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; done\\nexit 0\\n' > /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh", "chmod 755 /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh", "printf '[Unit]\\nDescription=DNS tuning\\nAfter=network-online.target irqbalance.service\\nWants=network-online.target\\nBefore=named.service\\n[Service]\\nType=oneshot\\nExecStart=/etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh\\nRemainAfterExit=yes\\n[Install]\\nWantedBy=multi-user.target\\n' > /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.service", "systemctl daemon-reload", "systemctl enable dnstune.service", "systemctl disable irqbalance", "cat /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh", "bash -n /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh", "sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=.*/GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\"mitigations=off\"/' /etc/default/grub", "update-grub"]
